GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows genuine fundamental improvement: Q1 2026 revenue +14.4% YoY to $17.23B, EPS +24.3% YoY to $17.55, operating margin expanding to ~37.7%, and ROE climbing to 14.7%. The franchise is structurally stronger post-consumer exit, with #1 M&A ranking, a record IB backlog, and the SpaceX IPO mandate reinforcing primacy. However, the market has already priced this aggressively: P/B at 2.48x is at the top of its 1-year range (1.6–2.5), PE at 16.8x is in the upper half of its 365-day range (13.0–18.4), and the stock is within 1.1% of its 52-week high. Balance-sheet leverage has risen from ~14.2x to ~16.8x assets/equity, increasing structural risk. The equity-risk premium over the 10-year Treasury is a thin 133bp. The SpaceX IPO mandate (June 2026) provides a credible near-term catalyst for fee income, but this is already partially reflected in the stock's 5.8% rally on the news. Net: strong trajectory and franchise quality are real, but valuation at the P/B ceiling caps the score at mildly attractive rather than strongly attractive.

Balance-sheet leverage increased from ~14.2x to ~16.8x assets/equity, amplifying downside risk in stress
SpaceX IPO mandate (2026-05-20) as lead underwriter for potential $75B+ June IPO — credible near-term fee catalyst
Strategic refocus on high-margin advisory/trading/AWM post-consumer exit; #1 global M&A ranking in 2025
